text: 🇲🇽📈 22.7 million formal jobs — an all-time record. Mexico closed June 2026 with 22,779,704 formal jobs registered at IMSS, the highest in history, with the daily wage base up 6.4% to 669 pesos. — Zoé Robledo, IMSS director, mañanera, July 8

🇲🇽✊ First in the OECD for minimum-wage recovery. They said wages couldn't rise without killing jobs. Since 2018 the minimum wage more than doubled in real terms — and formal employment just hit a record. "Mexico is in first place in minimum-wage recovery." — Édgar Amador, Treasury Secretary, mañanera, July 8

🇲🇽🏭 Record foreign investment, record trade — the numbers the "failed state" narrative ignores. Mexico captured $41 billion in foreign direct investment, and Mexico–US trade hit a record $839 billion. "Mexico and the United States trade more than ever." — Édgar Amador, Treasury Secretary, mañanera, July 8

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico won't trade principle for protocol on Peru. "With Ecuador, we broke relations because they invaded our embassy. In the case of Peru, they broke relations. Why? Because we said President Castillo is imprisoned illegally." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 8 Peru cut ties after Mexico refused to recognize Castillo's removal as legitimate.

🇲🇽🛢️ "I committed that there would be no gasolinazos, and we are keeping that promise." As the US–Iran conflict drives up global fuel prices, Sheinbaum said that without the government's measures a liter of gasoline would have hit 30 to 32 pesos. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 8

🔥🇲🇽 "The Mexican right doesn't love Mexicans. It doesn't love the people of Mexico." Sheinbaum answered an Argentine broadcaster's xenophobic remarks about Mexicans by pointing to who applauds them at home. "A pseudo-journalist... and this is the ally of the Mexican right." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 8

🚨🇲🇽 Mexico moves beyond diplomatic notes after ICE kills its citizens. "Our objective is to go beyond diplomatic notes. We cannot allow the mistreatment of our brothers and sisters in the United States." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 8 Sheinbaum instructed the Foreign Ministry to prepare new legal measures over the killing of Mexican migrants by ICE, calling them human rights violations.

🇲🇽📈 MEXICO–US TRADE HITS RECORD $839 BILLION AS INFLATION COOLS TO 3.6%

Two-way trade with the US reached an all-time high of $839 billion, cementing Mexico as America's number-one trading partner, while inflation eased to 3.6% and total exports hit $723 billion (+15.6% annualized). Finance Minister Edgar Amador noted the OECD ranks Mexico first in recovered purchasing power among member countries since 2021.

🌲🇲🇽 PROFEPA SHUTS DOWN ILLEGAL MINE AFTER INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES SPOKE UP

Federal environmental inspectors, backed by the Navy and state forest police, ordered the total closure of an illegal feldspar mine in Zacatlán, Puebla — operating with no environmental-impact permit and clearing protected Sierra Norte forest. The trigger: formal complaints from local Indigenous residents. Authorities are now reviewing all nine active mining concessions in the municipality.

🔥🇲🇽 "WE NEVER MAKE DEALS WITH CARTELS — WHO DOES?" SHEINBAUM FLIPS THE SCRIPT

Sheinbaum: "Mexico's government makes no agreements with cartel members... who negotiates with organized crime? We don't; we never will." She pointed the question back at US agencies — which granted Ovidio Guzmán benefits on July 25, 2024 — and at the PAN's Genaro García Luna, convicted in New York of taking Sinaloa Cartel money.
